description: Documented, evidenced bugs/caveats in reference tools. A reference exception requires: tool, song, category, and concrete evidence — never 'seems wrong'. Reference outputs are never patched; exceptions only explain deviations.

exceptions.reason: vgm2mid is codepage-sensitive: converting under Windows ANSI CP1252 vs CP932 yields different (non-identical) MIDI hashes for the same VGM. The VGMRips wiki warns that non-CP1252 codepages can corrupt timing. Demonstrated empirically (master-ninja): CP1252=9998eb62…, CP932=de0fde46…. The toolchain therefore pins en_US/CP1252 and treats that output as canonical; CP932 output is a documented reference anomaly, not ground truth.

arctic-wind.mid (397 B) and first-attack.mid (414 B) are near-empty outputs (a handful of events). Hypothesis (to be confirmed): vgm2mid's DAC/rhythm or chip handling simplified these short songs, or the VGM uses 2A03/ADPCM paths vgm2mid maps to very few notes. Recorded as an exception pending note-count analysis; the same-input comparison treats these as low-density fixtures.
